changes.detail: `StatusReturn` picked `code` from Elysia's `ElysiaStatus`, which Elysia 2.0.0-beta.21 removed (the status box now carries `status` and `response`). Every `status(...)` returned from an auth callback was a type error on that Elysia. `StatusReturn` now picks `status` and `response`, which every Elysia 2 beta has. Runtime behavior is unchanged. Also shipped as 0.85.1 for consumers pinned to 0.85.
changes.summary: Auth callbacks can return `status(...)` on Elysia 2.0.0-beta.21

changes.detail: The generated declarations of these exports list the same members in a different order (an optional `code` field moved within one object type). The types are identical; nothing to change in consuming code.
changes.summary: Generated declarations reordered without changing any type

migration.instruction: Apply identities/0003_canonical_account_compatibility or an equivalent application-journal migration before using native identity storage with UUID identity IDs. Pass --writer to committed CLI imports with a module exporting transactional writeAuthImport; preserve canonical IDs and put hashes in auth_credentials.

changes.summary: Widen native identity IDs for migrated accounts. Credential sign-in revokes the previous session. Committed CLI imports require an application writer instead of assuming users(sub,email,password).
Add canonical-account credential operations, UUID-referencing identity schemas, and durable session promotion for application-owned signup flows.
`trustedOrigins` also accepts a function of the request, so a multi-tenant app can decide per request (for example, allow only the request’s own origin) instead of listing every origin up front.
Use the chosen method name in TOTP QR account labels instead of internal user and factor identifiers. Preserve existing secrets and factor IDs.
Allow a default authenticator label resolved from the signed-in user when the submitted name is blank. Preserve custom names and pending enrollments.

docs/PERSISTENT-CREDENTIALS.md no longer mixes SQLite and PostgreSQL or gives stale migration advice: it has one complete PostgreSQL + Drizzle path and one SQLite path, the exact route list and session cookie, a typed guard, and current migration steps, and its code is typechecked against dist (check:guide) and run end to end in tests.

Preserve pending MFA login cookies during authentication-status and protected-route checks. Read-only session resolution no longer expires browser cookies, preventing delayed unauthenticated responses from erasing a newer login. Expired server sessions are still removed, and pending sessions remain unauthenticated.

migration.instruction: Run the mfa migration block before upgrading servers. Custom MFAStore implementations must add atomic claimCodeAttempt, completeCodeChallenge, and resetCodeAttempts methods. Handle HTTP 429 mfa_rate_limited responses with Retry-After and retryAfterMs. Recovery codes are opaque strings, not fixed eight-character values.

changes.summary: Replace permanent MFA lockouts with durable timed attempt budgets, independent recovery-code limits, and atomic recovery-code consumption. Previously locked accounts can authenticate again.

migration.instruction: Custom MFAStore implementations must implement atomic saveTotpEnrollment. Setup now resumes pending enrollments. TOTP verification preserves existing recovery codes; an empty backupCodes array means existing codes remain unchanged. First-issuance responses can be replayed for ten minutes after a valid TOTP using an encrypted receipt in factor JSON. No SQL migration is required.

changes.summary: Make TOTP setup and verification retry-safe across instances; preserve recovery codes when adding devices, resume pending QR codes, and include device labels in authenticator account names.

migration.instruction: Run mfa/0008_scoped_sms_challenges before rollout. Custom MFAStore implementations must implement getSmsChallengeStore with durable atomic state per user, pending session, and factor, and support the sms_send attempt budget. SMS codes issued by old servers must be requested again after upgrading.

changes.summary: Isolate SMS sign-in codes and resend cooldowns by pending session and phone. Preserve concurrent users codes and return structured resend timing. Keep a separate account delivery budget (default ten attempts per five minutes).

OAuth callbacks accept response_mode=form_post (Sign in with Apple): a POST to the callback route is re-issued as a same-site GET carrying only code, state, error, error_description and user, so SameSite=Lax state cookies are sent and the normal callback runs.

Optional persistent session cookies: `persistentCookie` on `instantiateUserSession` and `promoteToSession`, and `persistentSessionCookie` on the `webauthn` block, give the session cookie a Max-Age equal to the session length so a sign-in survives browser restarts. Without them the cookie still ends with the browser.

Passkey management: `GET`, `PATCH` (rename) and `DELETE` on `/auth/webauthn/credentials` for the signed-in user's own passkeys. Passkeys now have a `name` (webauthn migration 0003): the one passed at registration, or the provider's name from its AAGUID (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, Windows Hello, 1Password…). `hasOtherSignInMethod` can protect the last passkey. The client gains `passkeys.rename`, a working `passkeys.list`, `runPasskeyRegistration(client, { name })` and `runPasskeyAuthentication` for a sign-in button.

Sessions record how and where they signed in: `signInMethod` (provider name, `passkey`, `password`, `magic_link`, `otp`, `sso`) and the User-Agent (sessions migration 0003). `GET /auth/sessions` returns them with a coarse `device` (`{ browser, os }`) via `describeUserAgent`; pass the callback's new `request` to `instantiateUserSession` to record OAuth sign-ins. The client's `sessions.list` now returns the array the server sends.

Sign-in identities: several provider accounts can open one user. New `identities` config mounts `GET /auth/identities` and `DELETE /auth/identities/:id` (never removes the last way in unless `hasOtherSignInMethod` says so); `linkCallbackIdentity` links the OAuth callback's account to the signed-in user from `onLinkIdentity` and throws `AuthIdentityConflictError` when another user already owns it, so `onLinkIdentityConflict` finally runs. Postgres/Neon and in-memory stores; migration block `identities` creates `auth_identities` (compatible with existing app tables and the CLI importer) with a unique provider+subject index.

Invitations accept an optional invitee name and personal note: stored with the invitation (organizations migration 0002), passed to onSendInvitation, and the name is returned when listing invitations. Name is trimmed to 200 characters; the note keeps line breaks and is limited to 2,000.

Add per-grant refresh-token family inventory and revocation: optional `listFamilies`, `getFamily` and `revokeFamily` store methods (in-memory and Postgres/Neon, with a family index migration), and pass the family id to `getAccessTokenClaims` so resource servers can reject access tokens from a revoked device immediately.
Bind WebAuthn ceremonies to single-use server records, purpose, user and session; add a durable Postgres challenge store and prevent credential owner/key replacement or counter rollback.

Add encrypted interactive-transaction OAuth credential coordination; serialize refresh and removal with grant row locks, persist recovery before returning failures, and reject stale or forged credential handles. Bound ambiguous token renewals and require reconnection after permanent failures.
Declare session and linking cookies on the OAuth authorization route so opt-in session binding accepts existing signed-in users. Add an authorization-start regression test.
Add owner-bound encrypted linked-provider grant storage, session-bound OAuth linking, and an exported OAuth authorization resolver for separately consented connectors.
Allow authorized nonmember organization managers to list memberships. Revoke invitations when their delivery hook fails and return a sanitized retryable error.

migration.instruction: Configure organizations.getVerifiedEmail with provider-verified email evidence. Direct acceptInvitation callers must supply verifiedEmail. Custom OrganizationStore adapters must implement atomic acceptInvitation; older adapters fail closed.

changes.summary: Bind organization invitation acceptance to a verified email and atomically consume the invitation with membership creation. Deny expired, revoked, missing-organization and suspended-member invitations; preserve existing member roles.
Include Neon in the typed built-in provider registry and configuration resolution

migration.instruction: Move createNeonProviderConfiguration results from customProviders.neon to providersConfiguration.neon. Neon is now a built-in Citra provider; credentials, scopes and offlineAccess inputs are unchanged.

changes.summary: Use the native Citra Neon provider for Auth configuration and linked-account refresh
Add a Neon partner OAuth preset with S256 PKCE, explicit management scopes and opt-in offline access
Provide a Bun-native PostgreSQL migration entry point with transaction rollback, concurrency serialization and connection cleanup
Regenerate createAuthApplications and oidcProviderRoutes declarations with equivalent property ordering; accepted inputs and runtime behavior are unchanged
Expose a fixed-path sign-out subapp for directly inferred Eden clients and document Elysia 2 schema argument order
Provide fixed-route credentials APIs with inferred Eden request types and a package-owned manifest integration recipe
Document the required auth context session binding and protected account route
Delegate configurable credential routes through shared literal-path factories while retaining the same configuration and default endpoints
Document verified persistent credentials integration and correct Drizzle and migration APIs
Run auth setup according to the selected session store instead of always requiring PostgreSQL
Support existing Drizzle PostgreSQL clients for durable auth sessions

migration.instruction: Send client_credentials requests to /auth/api/token instead of /oauth2/token and update advertised enterprise token URLs. Keep authorization_code and refresh_token requests at /oauth2/token. Prefer auth({ oidc, apikeys }) for configuration validation. API-only consumers may explicitly keep tokenRoute: /oauth2/token if no OIDC handler uses that path.

changes.summary: Separate API credential token routes from OIDC and reject conflicting configuration
